First ionisation energy is the energy required to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of atoms in the gaseous state. 1
Electronegativity is the attraction exerted on a bonding pair of electrons. 1
The positive charge of the nucleus increases as you move left to right across the period (in addition to a decreased atomic radius). 1
Therefore, electrons are more attracted to the nucleus, and 1

Sodium has a low ionisation energy and chlorine has a high electronegativity. 1
Therefore electrons are transferred from sodium to chlorine, forming cations and anions (i.e. ionic bonding). 1
Chlorine gas consists of two non-metal atoms with high electronegativities. 1
Therefore electrons are shared, forming an uncharged covalent molecule. 1
Total 4
